# Slay the Cert — Talk Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Ship a 15-min talk "Slay the Cert" at a meetup on Wednesday 2026-06-03 — a public master HTML deck + a private branded variant + a rehearsed live alt-tab demo of the local dungeon.

**Architecture:** Single-file HTML deck generated by the `frontend-slides` Claude Code plugin (`Creative Voltage` preset), with two ~20-line custom JS hooks (card-stack reveal + achievement-pop). Demo runs from the existing dungeon dev server (`npm run dev` on `:5173`); base64-inlined GIF on slide 9 is the fallback. Public master committed to `public/talks/2026-06-03-slay-the-cert/slides.html`; branded variant + speaker notes gitignored.

**Tech Stack:** frontend-slides plugin (zarazhangrui), vanilla JS for custom animations, FFmpeg or screen-recorder + a small base64 inliner script (Python or Node one-liner) for the GIF fallback, Vite (existing) for the dungeon dev server, git for version control.

**Related documents:**
- Spec: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-25-slay-the-cert-talk-design.md`](../specs/2026-05-25-slay-the-cert-talk-design.md)
- Research: [`docs/superpowers/research/2026-05-25-slay-the-cert-talk-research.md`](../research/2026-05-25-slay-the-cert-talk-research.md)
- Project ship spec: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-18-slay-the-cert-gamification-design.md`](../specs/2026-04-18-slay-the-cert-gamification-design.md)

## Phase 4 — Custom JS hooks for animations (Day 7, ~4-5 hours)

### Task 4.1: Implement card-stack-reveal hook for Slide 3

**Files:**
- Modify: `public/talks/2026-06-03-slay-the-cert/slides.html` (add `<script>` block + class hooks on slide 3 elements)

- [ ] **Step 1: Add HTML structure for the cards**

Inside slide 3's container in `slides.html`, wrap each of the 5 montage screenshots in a `<div class="stack-card">` with sequential `data-stack-index` attributes (0 through 4). Example:

```html
<div class="slide" id="slide-3">
  <h2>AI slop in cert prep</h2>
  <div class="stack-container">
    <div class="stack-card" data-stack-index="0">
      <img src="assets/slop-montage/01-claudecertifications.png" alt="claudecertifications.com">
      <span class="brand-caption">claudecertifications.com</span>
    </div>
    <div class="stack-card" data-stack-index="1">...</div>
    <div class="stack-card" data-stack-index="2">...</div>
    <div class="stack-card" data-stack-index="3">...</div>
    <div class="stack-card" data-stack-index="4">...</div>
  </div>
  <p class="punchline" data-stack-index="5">Spot the difference?</p>
</div>
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Add CSS for the stacked-card visual**

Add to the inline `<style>` block of `slides.html`:

```css
.stack-container { position: relative; width: 600px; height: 400px; margin: 2em auto; }
.stack-card {
  position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%;
  opacity: 0; transform: translateX(100px) rotate(0deg);
  transition: opacity 400ms ease, transform 400ms ease;
}
.stack-card.visible { opacity: 1; transform: translateX(0) rotate(var(--stack-rotation, 0deg)); }
.stack-card:nth-child(1).visible { --stack-rotation: -3deg; }
.stack-card:nth-child(2).visible { --stack-rotation: 2deg; }
.stack-card:nth-child(3).visible { --stack-rotation: -2deg; }
.stack-card:nth-child(4).visible { --stack-rotation: 3deg; }
.stack-card:nth-child(5).visible { --stack-rotation: -1deg; }
.stack-card img { width: 100%; height: auto; box-shadow: 0 4px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.4); }
.brand-caption {
  position: absolute; bottom: 8px; right: 8px;
  background: rgba(0,0,0,.7); color: #fff; padding: 2px 8px;
  font-size: 0.8em; border-radius: 2px;
}
.punchline { opacity: 0; transition: opacity 400ms ease; text-align: center; font-size: 1.5em; }
.punchline.visible { opacity: 1; }
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the click-driven JS hook**

Append inside the existing `<script>` block of `slides.html` (or add a new `<script>` block before `</body>`):

```javascript
(function setupCardStack() {
  const slide = document.getElementById('slide-3');
  if (!slide) return;
  const cards = [...slide.querySelectorAll('[data-stack-index]')];
  let nextIndex = 0;
  function reveal() {
    if (nextIndex >= cards.length) return;
    cards[nextIndex].classList.add('visible');
    nextIndex += 1;
  }
  // Listen for click or Space/Right-arrow while slide 3 is active
  function isSlideActive() {
    return slide.classList.contains('active') || slide.classList.contains('current');
  }
  document.addEventListener('click', () => { if (isSlideActive()) reveal(); });
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    if (!isSlideActive()) return;
    if (e.key === ' ' || e.key === 'ArrowRight') {
      // Only intercept the keydown if we still have cards to reveal
      if (nextIndex < cards.length) { e.stopPropagation(); reveal(); }
    }
  });
})();
```

Note: the `isSlideActive` check uses both `.active` and `.current` because frontend-slides may use either — verify the actual class name by inspecting the live HTML before assuming.

- [ ] **Step 4: Manually test in browser**

Reload `slides.html`, navigate to slide 3.
- First click should reveal card 0.
- Second click reveals card 1.
- Third → card 2. Fourth → card 3. Fifth → card 4. Sixth → punchline.
- After 6 clicks, further clicks should advance to slide 4 (default presentation behavior).

If clicks advance the slide instead of revealing cards: the click handler isn't intercepting correctly. Fix by widening the `isSlideActive` check or adjusting `stopPropagation`.

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit card-stack hook**

```bash
git add public/talks/2026-06-03-slay-the-cert/slides.html && git commit -m "feat(talk): card-stack-on-click reveal animation for slide 3"
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the click-driven hook**

Append to the inline `<script>`:

```javascript
(function setupAchievementPop() {
  const slide = document.getElementById('slide-8');
  if (!slide) return;
  const items = [...slide.querySelectorAll('[data-pop-index]')]
    .sort((a, b) => parseInt(a.dataset.popIndex, 10) - parseInt(b.dataset.popIndex, 10));
  let nextIndex = 0;
  function pop() {
    if (nextIndex >= items.length) return;
    items[nextIndex].classList.add('popped');
    nextIndex += 1;
  }
  function isSlideActive() {
    return slide.classList.contains('active') || slide.classList.contains('current');
  }
  document.addEventListener('click', () => { if (isSlideActive()) pop(); });
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    if (!isSlideActive()) return;
    if (e.key === ' ' || e.key === 'ArrowRight') {
      if (nextIndex < items.length) { e.stopPropagation(); pop(); }
    }
  });
})();
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Test in browser**

Reload, navigate to slide 8. Each click should pop the next item in order (all 6 carrots first, then all 4 refused). After 10 clicks, next click advances to slide 9.

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit achievement-pop hook**


### Task 5.2: Inline the GIF as base64 into slide 9

**Files:**
- Create: `public/talks/2026-06-03-slay-the-cert/scripts/inline-gif.mjs`
- Modify: `public/talks/2026-06-03-slay-the-cert/slides.html`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the inliner script**

Create `public/talks/2026-06-03-slay-the-cert/scripts/inline-gif.mjs`:

```javascript
// Usage: node scripts/inline-gif.mjs
// Replaces the marker <!-- DUNGEON_DEMO_GIF --> in slides.html with a base64-encoded data: URI.
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { resolve, dirname } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const root = resolve(__dirname, '..');
const gifPath = resolve(root, 'assets/dungeon-demo.gif');
const htmlPath = resolve(root, 'slides.html');

const gif = readFileSync(gifPath);
const dataUri = `data:image/gif;base64,${gif.toString('base64')}`;

let html = readFileSync(htmlPath, 'utf8');
const marker = '<!-- DUNGEON_DEMO_GIF -->';
if (!html.includes(marker)) {
  console.error(`Marker ${marker} not found in slides.html. Add it inside slide 9 first.`);
  process.exit(1);
}

const replacement = `<img src="${dataUri}" alt="Dungeon boss fight demo loop" class="demo-fallback-gif">`;
html = html.replace(marker, replacement);
writeFileSync(htmlPath, html);
console.log(`Inlined ${gif.length.toLocaleString()} bytes of GIF into slides.html`);
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Add the marker to slide 9**

In `public/talks/2026-06-03-slay-the-cert/slides.html`, find slide 9 and add the marker inside the slide's content area:

```html
<div class="slide" id="slide-9">
  <h2 class="demo-cue">← live demo</h2>
  <div class="demo-fallback">
    <!-- DUNGEON_DEMO_GIF -->
    <p class="caption">(fallback loop — alt-tab to localhost:5173 for the live demo)</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

Add matching CSS:

```css
.demo-fallback-gif { max-width: 70%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 1em auto; border: 2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2); }
.demo-cue { text-align: center; font-size: 2em; opacity: .7; }
.demo-fallback .caption { text-align: center; font-style: italic; opacity: .5; font-size: .9em; }
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Run the inliner**

```powershell
node public\talks\2026-06-03-slay-the-cert\scripts\inline-gif.mjs
```
Expected: console output `Inlined NNN,NNN bytes of GIF into slides.html`. The `slides.html` file size jumps by ~(GIF size × 1.33) bytes.

- [ ] **Step 4: Verify in browser**

Reload `slides.html`, navigate to slide 9. Expected: the GIF loops in the slide. Close the dev server (`Ctrl+C` in the `npm run dev` terminal). Reload `slides.html` again — the GIF should STILL loop (because it's inlined, no network dependency).

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add public/talks/2026-06-03-slay-the-cert/scripts/inline-gif.mjs public/talks/2026-06-03-slay-the-cert/slides.html && git commit -m "feat(talk): base64-inline boss-fight GIF into slide 9 as demo fallback"
```

## Phase 7 — Polish (Days 13-15, ~3 hours total)

### Task 7.1: Tone-check every slide

**Files:**
- Modify: `public/talks/2026-06-03-slay-the-cert/slides.html`

- [ ] **Step 1: Read every slide aloud, listening for snark**

Per the spec, the tone is "Senior-Manager-appropriate, critique without snark." Red flags:
- Any word that sounds like a put-down ("garbage", "lazy", "scam")
- Any judgment of the people behind the slop sites (criticize the *pattern*, not the *people*)
- Any superlative claim about the user's own work ("the best", "revolutionary")

- [ ] **Step 2: Fix every flagged line**

Replace with analytical-neutral phrasing. Example transformations:
- "AI slop" → "AI-generated lookalikes" (in body copy; the title "Slay the Cert" can stay punchy)
- "they all just copy each other" → "the same template appears across vendors"
- "my game is amazing" → "real users got value from it" (and let the testimonials do the work)

- [ ] **Step 3: Commit tone-check pass**
